title: His father's view of drink and Freeman's own health habits
summary: Freeman's athletic father disapproved of Tough's and McPartland's drinking; Freeman and his brother kept to health, golf and moderation.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: When I say we are all sick, I think that I was very much influenced and frightened by my father who was an athletic man, and thought it was a thought it was a sin to drink sin to destroy oneself. He loved Dave Tuft and Jimmy Tough McPartland. They were at our home all the time, but he
felt very badly, he could not condone their drinking habits. They were not addicts ever. Never got into that. But a very interesting point, that our era had none of that.
It was an thing to know,

Incredible. But we were all drinkers. I was not -- I never really got into drinking a great deal because, by having been an athlete as a child, I loved the idea of health and my father instilled this in me, and kept -- my brother to this day is a health nut or a nutter as they say in England, and I suppose I am too. We don't overeat, we don't eat a great deal, we are not big drinkers, although I do like a couple of drinks every day.

I am a golfer, my brother is very active in what he does. He takes long walks. We're really concerned with health. But I don't think that Dave Tough and George Wettling and many of the musicians we were raised with were concerned with that and they thought it was kind of corny. Although Dave Tough did play a little golf.
